content: Currently, the publication does not include information on Cuban cigars due to the Cuban embargo. It provides detailed specifications and information about each cigar, as well as general knowledge about cigars, such as wrapper colors, shapes, and sizes. There is an Almanac section that lists new brands and those discontinued since the last edition. It also includes details about ancient brands still in production, a list of unusual cigars (such as those with multicolored wrappers), and a catalog of the smallest and largest cigars available, categorized by length and ring gauge. The first edition of this publication was released in 1995 and covered 370 brands. The latest edition, published in 2007, expanded to include information on 1,233 brands, comprising 1,074 handmade cigars, 94 machine-made cigars, and 65 small cigars or cigarillos. There is also a companion edition titled Perelman's Pocket Cyclopedia of Havana Cigars, which focuses exclusively on Cuban cigar brands. This edition is currently in its third iteration, published in 2005, but it is not updated annually (the second edition was published in 1998). It includes information on how cigars are made in Cuba, the history of tobacco and Cuban brands, and details about vitolas (cigar sizes and shapes). Both editions are authored by Richard B. Perelman.
